label: GitHub Copilot CLI

skills.note: Copilot CLI's own location. It would also read .claude/skills, but DAW does not make one tool depend on another tool's directory.

agents._model_note: Deliberately NOT emitted, and this note is the check's evidence that the omission is a decision. Copilot's .agent.md does take `model`, but its values are concrete ids and family aliases — there is no `inherit` — and an unset field falls to per-agent-type defaults plus server-side experiments (measured live, 2026-08-25: the session on one model, every DAW subagent on another, no signal in the UI; their issue #3824 documents the routing and #2758 the silent cost downgrade). Pinning a concrete model here would override the user's session choice on every install, which is worse than the nondeterminism it removes. If GitHub ships an inherit value, emit `{model}` like the other adapters and delete this note.

hooks_note: The scripts land in the repo; the manifest that points at them does NOT. GitHub's hooks reference says policy hooks are available 'regardless of folder trust state' — the others are not. Repository hooks load only in a folder the user has trusted, and trust is answered in a dialog `copilot -p` cannot show. Measured 2026-08-22/23 with trustedFolders as the only variable: trusted, 3 hooks ran and the write was refused; not trusted, 0 ran and the file was written; user-level, refused either way. The trap is that trust is invisible — the repo a developer has used interactively is trusted and enforces, the same repo on CI is not and does not. install.sh writes ~/.copilot/hooks/daw.json instead, once per machine, pointing at each repo's scripts by relative path. Not both levels: where the folder is trusted the reference says every source is combined and all run, so two levels judge every write twice.

choice_prompt.note: the ask_user tool — agent and Plan mode; absent in Ask mode
